name: Dry Road Sword Primer (Hạn Lộ Kiếm Quyết)
concept: The caravan guard's method, taught to the outer gate on the hot steppe roads below the valley. It draws Metal from the ore hills and Fire from the noon ground, either one, and keeps a sword arm loose through a long day's heat. It fights in short exchanges and gets stronger the longer the guard has been on the road.
lore: Written by the second head Liễu Hành Vân for the companies she hired out to the camel trains of Đà Đội Thôn, so that a girl from the hot springs and a boy from the copper mines could learn the same sword.

name: Contract Sword Canon (Khế Kiếm Kinh)

effects.name: Serve a Term
effects.rule: Each pulse you are Pressing (or evade an attack, at most 1 per pulse) and landed no art hit serves 1 Term (Khoản); each enemy art hit you take strikes 1 Term off.

concept: A hired sword's method: it counts a fight as a contract counts its terms to the fee. The cultivator counts terms instead of breaths. In a fight, each second you are Pressing and strike nothing serves a Term (Khoản 款), and each hit you take strikes one Term off. It is a method for finishing a contract, not for winning a war.
lore: The founder Quách Lĩnh Thù's method, the canon every inner disciple of the valley takes before their first contract. The founder cut his saying on the lintel of the hall, where every hired sword passes under it on the way out: the fee is the whole of the thanks.

name: Brushed Sleeve Step (Phất Y Bộ)
concept: The founder's own art, the valley's custom made into a step: a sleeve brushed across the hilt ends the hire. It runs on Wind alone. The holder moves on the air between one step and the next, and a sleeve brushed across a blade turns it. Taught only to a Wind root; the valley has had two in six centuries.
lore: Quách Lĩnh Thù taught it to no one and left it folded into his grey robe in the valley's hall when he walked away in 790. The robe opens only to a Wind root. Liễu Hành Vân, who had no Wind, kept it closed for three centuries because no one had the Wind to open it, until a hawk-catcher's son from Thương Ưng Đài did: Thang Vô Tạ.
